name: ui_event_stream
doc: Opt-in async UI event stream (cycle-free). Single-subscriber.

name: BotFilterCardStyle
doc:
Card-style choice. Mirrors Kotlin `CardStyle` (`OKComponents/core/OKTradeCore/trade_core/
src/main/java/com/okinc/unify_trade/bot/list/CardStyle.kt:9-12`) in declaration order.

Crosses the FFI as an enum, not a string. The *persisted* form stays the Kotlin enum
`name` — `SpStyleRepositoryImpl` writes `CardStyle.name` and seven native call sites read
it back, so this type must not become the persistence format.

Legacy also maps these to analytics vocabulary that differs from both spellings
(`DETAILED → "full"`, `NO_IMAGE → "compact"`, `MINI → "mini"`). That mapping stays native
and is already duplicated twice inside the sheet — do not add a third copy here.

name: SmartArbitrageCoinPickerSegment
doc:
Mirrors legacy `SmartArbitrageSegment` (`SmartArbitrageAssetType.kt:17-27`)
— the segment chip filter. `accepts()` has no Rust equivalent anywhere
before this file (manifest Amendment II); ported additively, from
scratch, without touching the Kotlin file.

name: SignalBotLeverConfig
doc:
The leverage-config triple the "adjust leverage" dialog renders.

`percents` is a CSV string (native `leveragePercents` shape); the
lever-interval source returns `Vec<String>` and is joined with `,` before
reaching the merge.

name: set_state_observer
doc:
Set a state observer (UniFFI export).

DEPRECATED: callback-based observer. Use `state_stream()` —
the callback observer pins the foreign object in UniFFI's
static handleMap and produces a cross-language retain cycle
(Android GC + iOS ARC).

name: release
doc:
Stop-gap teardown (TEMPORARY — target state is the stream APIs,
which need no teardown call).

One idempotent call at host lifecycle end that breaks the
UniFFI handleMap cycle for any registered callback observers,
ends active streams, and stops effects. On Kotlin call BEFORE
`destroy()`. Includes `stop()`.

name: state_stream
doc:
Opt-in async state-change stream (cycle-free, signal-only).
Single-subscriber, latest-wins. `changed()` resolves `true` on
change (pull `state()` for the snapshot), `false` when the
interactor is released or a newer subscription replaces this one.
